sections.label: Expanding criminal legal aid coverage
sections.summary: MinLaw study shows households below S$1,500 monthly PCHI struggle to afford representation, so coverage expands from the 25th to 35th percentile and to all criminal offences with exceptions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: A study conducted by MinLaw showed that accused persons whose monthly per capita household income, or PCHI, is less than S$950 cannot afford legal representation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Those whose monthly PCHI is less than S$1,500, or around the 35th percentile, will also find it challenging to afford representation even for plead guilty cases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Thus, we are expanding our coverage from the 25th to the 35th percentile of households by income.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: We will, at the same time, increase aid coverage to all criminal offences, with some exceptions.

sections.label: Hong Kong legal aid costs
sections.summary: He cited Hong Kong spending S$217 million on criminal and civil legal aid in 2016 as an example of escalating costs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: He mentioned an example of escalating costs in Hong Kong.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: They spent S$217 million on criminal and civil legal aid in 2016.

sections.label: Criminal defence aid for SCPRs
sections.summary: The Bill provides criminal defence aid to needy Singaporean Citizens and Permanent Residents charged with offences not excluded by the Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Bill provides for criminal defence aid to be granted to needy Singaporean Citizens and Permanent Residents, or SCPRs, who are charged with offences not excluded by the Bill.

sections.label: Capital cases under LASCO
sections.summary: Coverage widens to all criminal offences with specific exceptions in four classes, including capital cases covered by LASCO, administered by the Supreme Court.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: As mentioned earlier, we will widen our coverage to all criminal offences with specific exceptions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: These exceptions fall into four classes of offences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: These are capital cases that will continue to be covered by LASCO, the Legal Assistance Scheme for Capital Offences, which is administered by the Supreme Court.

sections.label: Private prosecutions exception
sections.summary: Fourth, the exceptions include private prosecutions that have not been taken up by the Public Prosecutor.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Fourth, private prosecutions that have not been taken up by the Public Prosecutor.

sections.label: Raising PCHI income threshold
sections.summary: The income criterion is the monthly PCHI threshold, raised from S$950 to S$1,500 when the PDO commences operations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The income criterion is the monthly PCHI threshold, which will be raised from S$950 to S$1,500 when the PDO commences operations.

sections.label: Criminal defence aid and penalties
sections.summary: The Bill provides fines up to S$5,000 or six months' imprisonment, and enables the Public Defender's Office to provide criminal defence aid to vulnerable persons.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: For such cases, the Bill provides for a fine not exceeding S$5,000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months, or to both.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Bill will enable the Public Defender's Office to provide criminal defence aid, which will enhance access to justice for the more vulnerable members of society.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Justice should not only be the preserve of those who can afford lawyers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: It should be accessible to those without the means to do so.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: This is a measure of how far we have come and how caring and compassionate we are as a society.

sections.label: Bill formalises legal representation arrangement
sections.summary: The Bill formalises the arrangement for the Government to provide legal representation to accused persons of limited means in criminal proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The introduction of this Bill represents an important development in this quest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It formalises the arrangement for provision of legal representation by the Government to accused persons of limited means in criminal proceedings.

sections.label: Public Defender's Office announced and Bill introduced
sections.summary: In April 2022 the Minister for Law announced a Public Defender's Office for indigent accused persons, and the Bill was introduced in July 2022 after consultations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Sixteen years later in April 2022, the hon Minister for Law finally announced the Government's decision to set up a Public Defender's Office for indigent accused persons in certain criminal proceedings that will be co-funded by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This was described as yet another significant shift.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This Bill was then introduced in July 2022, after extensive consultations.

sections.label: Funding defence and rule of law commitment
sections.summary: Funding defence of accused persons costs serious money, and setting up the PDO and providing criminal aid is a commitment to enhance the rule of law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It does cost serious money to fund the defence of accused persons and we heard the hon Senior Parliamentary Secretary mention about the Hong Kong experience just now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: We all agreed that the set-up of the PDO and the provision of criminal aid to indigent accused persons is a commitment we have to make to enhance the rule of law in Singapore.

sections.label: Support for PCHI coverage
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Ministry's intent to cover accused persons in households with a PCHI of $1,500 or lower.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In this regard, I support the Ministry's intent to cover accused persons in households with a PCHI of $1,500 or lower.

sections.label: Definition of Court and proceedings
sections.summary: Clause 2 defines "Court" widely to include any Court of competent jurisdiction, and "proceedings" as those in clause 8(1) or 12(8).

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First on the definition of "Court" appearing in clause 2 of the Bill, I note that it is widely defined to include any Court of competent jurisdiction before which any "proceedings" are heard. "Proceedings" is defined as proceedings mentioned in clause 8(1) or 12(8) of the Bill which deals with circumstances in which a grant of aid may be issued.

sections.label: Public Defenders and mentally ill accused
sections.summary: A Member asks how the Public Defender will deal with an accused person with mental illness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Second, may I ask how will the PD deal with an accused with mental illness?

sections.label: Mental incapacity, minors and aid cancellation
sections.summary: A Member asks how Public Defenders will deal with mentally ill accused without empowering provisions, and asks the Senior Parliamentary Secretary to outline circumstances for cancelling the Grant of Aid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This is, with respect, a little bit incongruous, because there is no legal difference in the situation between a minor and a mentally incapacitated person in that both of them cannot act on their own.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I seek a clarification from the hon Senior Parliamentary Secretary as to how she proposes that the PDs deal with accused with mental illnesses in the absence of the empowering provisions in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: If I am right, may I ask the hon Senior Parliamentary Secretary to outline the prescribed circumstances she has in mind for the purposes of cancellation of the Grant of Aid bearing in mind the aims of this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Once this Bill is passed, the Government will both prosecute and defend its citizens – there will be no contradiction if we see both acts as necessary for the pursuit of justice and protection of the public good.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The public prosecutors are not vengeful vigilantes but impartial officers of the state.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: They are not activists or lobbyists for specific causes, but advocates presenting the best defence possible for their clients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Together, these officers – prosecutors and defenders – make for a true commitment to the rule of law in Singapore.

sections.label: Income percentile coverage of PDO scheme
sections.summary: The Minister for Law said the PDO scheme would cover up to the 35th income percentile, raising the per capita household income cut-off from $950 to $1,500.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Minister for Law had informed the House in April this year that while the current CLAS scheme was able to cover applicants up to the 25th income percentile, the PDO scheme would cover up to the 35th income percentile of resident households.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Minister stated then that the per capita household income cut-off would be raised from $950 to $1,500.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary confirmed this earlier and this is a significant inclusive change.

sections.label: Public Defender powers and merits for aid
sections.summary: A Member asks what powers the Chief PD or PDO officers have to access Government information, locate witnesses or compel their attendance for interviews.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Next, on the issue of merits for aid, clause 12(2) provides that the Chief PD could consider factors such as whether the proceedings might involve the tracing, interviewing or cross-examination of witnesses on behalf of the applicant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This raises an important issue regarding the power of Public Defenders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Could I ask what powers the Chief PD or other officers of the PDO would have to access Government information, to locate witnesses or to compel their attendance for interviews?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is further provided in clause 3(7) that every Public Defender who is not a public officer is deemed to be a public servant within the meaning of the Penal Code when carrying out his PD functions.

sections.label: Minister's direction to give aid
sections.summary: Clause 12(7) enables the Minister to direct that aid be given even where the applicant does not satisfy the requirements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Despite the requirements to qualify for aid set out in the Bill, clause 12(7) enables the Minister to direct that aid be given even in cases where the applicant does not satisfy the requirements.

sections.label: Aid for excluded offences
sections.summary: A Member asks the Ministry to confirm that the Minister's residual power under clause 12(7) does not extend to aid for excluded offences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry confirm that the Minister's residual power under clause 12(7) does not extend to providing aid for excluded offences?

sections.label: Capital cases and Public Defenders
sections.summary: A Member asks whether the matter was broached with the Supreme Court and why capital cases were excluded from the PDO.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry inform the House whether this matter was broached with the Supreme Court and why the decision was taken not to include capital cases under the PDO?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The PD scheme has the potential to go some way towards addressing the imbalance of power and resources between the state prosecution and an accused person.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I welcome the introduction of the Public Defenders Bill.

sections.label: Solicitor duty to disclose
sections.summary: Clause 4(5) states a solicitor has a duty to disclose information to the Chief Public Defender despite solicitor-client privilege.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Clause 4(5) of the Bill states that despite any privilege arising out of the relationship between solicitor and client, a solicitor has a duty to disclose any information to the Chief Public Defender (CPD) which may enable the CPD to perform his functions under the Act.

sections.label: Exclusion from solicitor panel
sections.summary: Clause 5(1) provides for the exclusion of a solicitor from the panel of solicitors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Next, clause 5(1) of the Bill provides for the exclusion of a solicitor from the panel of solicitors.

sections.label: Grant of criminal defence aid
sections.summary: Clause 12 sets out the process for grant of criminal defence aid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Clause 12 of the Bill sets out the process for grant of criminal defence aid.

sections.label: Aid for more than one person
sections.summary: A Member asks the Senior Parliamentary Secretary to clarify why aid should not be granted to more than one person in the same proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: For clause 14(2), can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary clarify why aid should not be granted to more than one person in the same set of proceedings?

sections.label: Aid for dangerous driving offences
sections.summary: A Member urges the Senior Parliamentary Secretary to consider allowing criminal defence aid for persons accused of dangerous driving where sentences may entail imprisonment of a few years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: For the excluded offences under the Schedule, while I understand the need to exclude offences for most traffic offences or most regulatory offences, may I urge the Senior Parliamentary Secretary to consider allowing criminal defence aid to persons accused of dangerous driving where the sentences may entail imprisonment of a few years?

sections.label: Public Defender independence and policy change
sections.summary: MP asks the Senior Parliamentary Secretary to confirm the Public Defender's Office will be fully independent and to clarify what caused the policy change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: And the Minister had said, "The policy of the Government is not to grant legal aid in criminal cases except for cases involving capital punishment".

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: And in his speech, Prof Jayakumar said that, "It is incongruous and inconsistent that public funds should be used to defend an accused person which the state has decided ought to be charged in Court and to use public funds at the same time to get him off." Sir, in the interest of transparency, since the Public Defender comes under MinLaw and prosecution by the Police comes under MHA, may I ask Senior Parliamentary Secretary to confirm that the Public Defender's Office (PDO) will be given full independence to represent their accused in Court without concern that the state is incurring public funds to prosecute the accused person.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary also clarify what brought about this change in the policy?

sections.label: Solicitor duty to disclose information
sections.summary: Clause 4(5) states the solicitor has a duty to disclose information that may otherwise be subject to client-attorney privilege to the Chief PD.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, I note that clause 4(5) of the Bill states that the solicitor has a duty to disclose information which may otherwise be subject to client-attorney privilege, the Chief PD (CPD) to enable the CPD to perform its functions under the Act.

sections.label: Eligibility for Public Defender's Office
sections.summary: Clause 12(1)(b) states only Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents are eligible to apply to the PDO.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Clause 12(1)(b) of the Bill states that only Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents are eligible to apply to the PDO.

sections.label: Formal appeals mechanism for aid refusal
sections.summary: The passage suggests considering a formal appeals mechanism for an accused person to appeal the Chief PD's decision not to grant aid.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While there may be reasons for this different approach, we should consider having a formal appeals mechanism for an accused person to appeal against the CPD's decision not to grant them aid for greater certainty.

sections.label: Recruitment plans and information safeguards
sections.summary: MP asks about specific recruitment plans for the PDO and safeguards preventing unauthorised use or disclosure of information if an officer is reassigned.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While the Ministry has previously stated that the PDO hopes to recruit across a mixture of backgrounds, what is its specific plans to address the concerns raised by the criminal bar and could the Minister elaborate on what will be done to ensure that talented young and mid-career lawyers would consider public defence and even private criminal defence work as their first choice.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If so, what safeguards would there be in place to ensure that any information obtained by a Public Defender is safeguarded from unauthorised use or disclosure if the officer is subsequently reassigned or rotated into another office, such as that of the Public Prosecutor's office.

sections.label: Public funds and judicial confidence
sections.summary: The passage states justice must be done and seen to be done, and notes public questions about expanding public funds for a Public Defender's Office.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This was a key point of our Motion raised in November 2020 and all of us would agree that in order to maintain confidence in our judicial system, justice must be done and also must be seen to be done.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: There will be questions from the public about whether public funds should be expanded to fund a Public Defender's Office, especially in the case where the accused person is, in fact, guilty of a crime.

sections.label: Public Defenders as officers
sections.summary: Public Defenders are officers of the Court and Public Officers under clause 3 of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is also helpful to note at this point, that Public Defenders are officers of the Court.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: They are also Public Officers pursuant to clause 3 of the Bill.

sections.label: PDO formation positive development
sections.summary: Despite concerns and requests for clarification, the Member says the Ministry's formation of the PDO is a positive development.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While I have touched on some areas of concern and asked for some clarifications in my speech today, it does not take away that the formation of the PDO by the Ministry is a positive development.

sections.label: Criminal legal aid income eligibility
sections.summary: The Member proposes raising the per capita gross monthly household income eligibility from $1,500 to $2,200, noting the Chief Public Defender can require co-payment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Minister Shanmugam has proposed in his Ministerial Statement in April, to peg the eligibility for criminal legal aid at a per capita gross monthly household income of $1,500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We are of the view that this amount should be raised to $2,200, which is in line with our recommendation for Singapore to adopt a minimum living wage of $2,200 for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government may argue that this would unnecessarily drive up costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, we note that this Bill gives the Chief Public Defender the right to require applicants to co-pay for the legal costs.

sections.label: Access to justice eligibility criteria
sections.summary: The Member supports the Bill and proposes pegging criminal legal aid eligibility to a per capita gross monthly household income of $2,200.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Increasing access to justice cannot be measured in dollars and cents and every person should have a chance to present his best case in court with legal representation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Hence, while we support the Bill, we also propose that the eligibility criteria for criminal legal aid be pegged to a per capita gross monthly household income of $2,200.

sections.label: PDO legal aid scope and cap
sections.summary: The PDO provides legal aid with a $1,500 income cap, expands coverage to non-capital charges with listed exclusions, and allows assistance in exceptional circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The PDO will ensure legal aid for vulnerable citizens and permanent residents who are charged but do not have the financial means to hire a lawyer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The new programme will set the income cap at the 35th percentile, which would cap the defendant's per capita household monthly income at $1,500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I think this cap is quite reasonable and it is a good beginning as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I also support the expansion of criminal legal aid to include all non-capital charges, but not private prosecutions not handled by the Attorney-General, gambling, organised crime and terrorism, as well as traffic summons and certain charges such as littering and illegal parking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am reassured that the Attorney-General has given the Minister the power to authorise the Chief Public Defender to grant assistance to ineligible applicants who are facing exceptional circumstances.

sections.label: Public Defenders Bill purpose
sections.summary: The Public Defenders Bill seeks to enact and enshrine in legislation Government-funded criminal legal aid for persons meeting means testing and other criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Public Defenders Bill seeks to enact and enshrine in legislation criminal legal aid, funded by the Government, for persons who meet the means testing and other criteria.

sections.label: CLAS application processing time
sections.summary: CLAS currently takes about two weeks to consider an application, and clause 12(4) provides an expedited process for urgent cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By way of comparison, CLAS currently takes about two weeks to consider an application.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I note also that for urgent cases – and this is something that the hon Senior Parliamentary Secretary mentioned – clause 12(4) does provide for an expedited process.

sections.label: CLAS case numbers 2020 2021
sections.summary: CLAS undertook 864 cases in 2020 and 775 cases in 2021, figures obtained from CLAS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As a rough measure, CLAS undertook 864 cases in 2020 and 775 cases in 2021, figures of which I had obtained from CLAS.

sections.label: Questions on PDO clauses
sections.summary: The member asks whether the PDO can take appeals or applications in originating proceedings, refer cases to external bodies, and grant aid in private prosecutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On clause 8(1)(b), which sets out the scope of criminal defence aid, I would like to ask the hon Senior Parliamentary Secretary whether the PDO can take up appeals or criminal applications where the PDO had not represented the accused person in the originating proceedings, which are provided for in clause 8(1)(a).

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On clause 12(5), which provides that the PDO may, instead of approving an application, refer it to a body or organisation providing pro bono legal services, I would like to ask the hon Senior Parliamentary Secretary whether the PDO will be able to refer cases to an external body if the applicant does not meet all the criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On clause 14(2), which provides that the PDO must not act for more that one accused person, appellant, respondent or party in the same proceedings, the hon Senior Parliamentary Secretary mentioned that the PDO could refer these cases to CLAS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, if the defending party is unable to afford their own lawyers, they are essentially in the same position as regards the inequality of arms as a person who is charged by the Public Prosecutor and they would face the same sentences if they were convicted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, would the Ministry consider allowing for the Public Defender to grant aid in private prosecutions prosecuted by lawyers where the defending party meets the eligibility criteria?

sections.label: Legal aid cost studies Canada Australia
sections.summary: In Canada, unequal access to justice costs were estimated at about 2.35 times annual direct legal aid expenditures; Australian studies show net public benefits from legal assistance expenditures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In Canada, the cost of unequal access to justice on public spending in other areas, like social assistance and healthcare costs, had been estimated to be about 2.35 times more than the annual direct service expenditures on legal aid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In Australia, studies have shown that there are net public benefits from legal assistance expenditures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Investments in legal aid can lead to significant Government savings through avoided cost of arrest, conviction, incarceration, probation and post-prison supervision.

sections.label: False statement offence penalties
sections.summary: Clause 23 offences involving false or misleading statements carry the same fines of S$5,000 per contravention and imprisonment of up to six months as section 21 of the Legal Aid and Advice Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Next, in relation to offences involving false or misleading statement, the Offences and Penalties proposed under clause 23 of this Bill, is the same as that of section 21 of the Legal Aid and Advice Act, in that both carry fines of S$5,000 per contravention and imprisonment of up to six months.

sections.label: US felony plea bargain rates
sections.summary: In the US, the vast majority of felony convictions result from plea bargains: some 94% at the state level and 97% at the federal level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In the US, the vast majority of felony convictions are now the result of plea bargains: some 94% at the state level, 97% at the federal level.

sections.label: US criminal justice spending
sections.summary: Of US$200 billion spent by state and local governments on criminal justice in 2008, only 2% went to indigent defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Of the US$200 billion spent on criminal justice activities by state and local governments in 2008, only 2% went to indigent defence.

sections.label: Public Defenders versus appointed counsel
sections.summary: A Yale Law Journal study of almost 2,500 Philadelphia cases found Public Defenders reduced murder conviction rate by 19% and life sentence probability by 62%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In an article published in Yale Law Journal which involved a study of almost 2,500 cases in Philadelphia, it was found that in comparison to appointed counsel, Public Defenders had reduced the clients' murder conviction rate by 19%, lowered the probability that their clients receive a life sentence by 62%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Public Defenders also reduced overall expected time served in prison by 24%.

sections.label: PDO and Criminal Legal Aid Scheme
sections.summary: The PDO will collaborate with the Criminal Legal Aid Scheme, which provides criminal legal assistance for the vulnerable and covers offences under 17 statutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, the PDO will collaborate with the Criminal Legal Aid Scheme, which similarly provides criminal legal assistance for the vulnerable and covers offences under 17 statutes, such as the Penal Code, Vandalism Act and the Women's Charter.

sections.label: Jail terms under statutes
sections.summary: Section 22 of the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act provides jail terms up to two years, and section 131 of the Road Traffic Act up to six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For instance, the general offence provisions under section 22 of the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act provides for jail terms of up to two years to be imposed for certain cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The general offences and penalties provision under section 131 of the Road Traffic Act provides for jail terms of up to six months to be imposed for certain cases.

sections.label: Perceived conflict of interest
sections.summary: Even without actual conflict, perceived conflict may be damaging, given the Government's previous position on prosecuting and paying for defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Even if there is no actual conflict, there may still be perceived conflict, which can be equally as damaging.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: There is some basis for concerns about conflict given that the Government's position previously was that it may not make sense for the Government to be both prosecuting the accused and paying for the defence.

sections.label: Public Defender's Office plan
sections.summary: The plan to set up the Public Defender's Office raises the income limit of applicants and expands support to cover most offences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The latest plan to set up the Public Defender's Office (PDO) is the next significant step by the Government in facilitating adequate and easier access to justice for more vulnerable Singaporeans and permanent residents by raising the income limit of applicants to cover more of limited means and expanding the scope of support to cover most offences.

sections.label: Discretion for excluded offences aid
sections.summary: Speaker seeks clarification on allowing the Chief PD or Minister discretion to grant aid for offences in 10 statutes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In these aspects, I wish to seek the following clarifications.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: However, rather than having a total blanket exclusion for those of the offences listed in the 10 specific statutes, can we explore the flexibility to enable either the Chief PD or the Minister to exercise discretion to grant aid due to special circumstances when he or she is of the opinion that it is in the best interest of the justice to do so.

sections.label: Shared records and PDO staffing
sections.summary: Speaker asks about shared applicant records and the optimal number of Public Defenders and support staff for the PDO.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: With this, each applicant's record will be visible to both entities, reducing the time needed to verify if the applicant has previously received aid in either of the schemes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I also wish to inquire about the optimal number of Public Defenders and support staff required to ensure smooth operations of the PDO and whether the Ministry is on track with the recruitment to reach this target when the PDO begins operations by the end of 2022.

sections.label: Public Defender qualifications and training
sections.summary: Speaker asks what the Chief PD considers duly qualified and experienced, and whether training will be provided.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In this regard, I wish to inquire what would be considered by the Chief PD as duly qualified and experienced to carry out duties as Public Defenders and whether adequate training will be provided to fresh graduates and young lawyers before they are assigned to take on cases independently.

sections.label: Income criteria and aid discretion
sections.summary: Passage notes the Minister or PDO can grant aid outside income criteria, and discusses the $1,500 per capita income cap.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In this Bill, the Minister or the PDO have the power to grant aid to applicants who do not meet the monthly income criteria under certain circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: One Member proposed to increase the per capita monthly income cap to $2,200.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The $1,500 per capita proposed by MinLaw is equivalent to $6,000 total household income for a 4-person household.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We must exercise caution when deciding whether this power should be used.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We should not forget the objective of this Bill is to help those accused who cannot afford legal representation.

sections.label: Income ceiling and conflict of interest
sections.summary: Passage describes the Bill's income ceiling of $1,500 per household member and clause 14(2) on conflicts of interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This Public Defenders Bill aims to provide just that for Singapore Citizens and PRs who meet the criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I understand that the income ceiling will be set at the bottom 35% of households, whose income per household member is $1,500 or lower.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Is it still too low a ceiling, considering that a three- or four-member household who is just above that ceiling would still struggle to pay legal fees ranging between $5,000 and $8,000 that private lawyers may charge for simple criminal defence matters?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: To avoid conflicts of interest, clause 14(2) of the Bill rightly provides that the PDO must not act for more than one accused person or party in the same proceedings.

sections.label: Review of excluded offences schedule
sections.summary: Speaker asks how often the Ministry will review the Schedule of excluded offences under clause 8(3).

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As clause 8(3) of the Bill allows the Minister to amend the Schedule of excluded offences, how often will the Ministry review the list of excluded offences and potentially reduce some of the exclusions, so that more people can benefit?

sections.label: PDO operations and outsourcing
sections.summary: PDO is targeted to commence operations in end of 2022, starting with PDO-employed lawyers taking all cases before considering outsourcing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Moving on to the operational and structural aspects of the PDO, I understand that PDO is targeted to commence operations in end of 2022, and the aim is to start by having PDO-employed lawyers take on all of PDO's cases before PDO considers outsourcing cases to qualified lawyers at a later stage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: When PDO commences operations, how many more people will be able to receive full legal representation, compared to the present average of 1,400 people who receive full legal representation every year under CLAS?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Another question I have is, what are the conditions to be satisfied before PDO will consider outsourcing cases to qualified lawyers in private practice?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Is the intention for the remuneration payable to external lawyers under clause 6 of the Bill to be fixed under subsidiary regulations or will that be subject to another consultation?

sections.label: CLAS and PDO overlap
sections.summary: Asks whether redundancies exist if an applicant eligible for both CLAS and PDO can receive the same aid from both.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For instance, if an applicant is eligible for both CLAS and PDO, that is, if both offences are non-capital offences under the Penal Code and if the applicant qualifies under both means test, will there be redundancies to have both CLAS and PDO capable of providing the same aid?

sections.label: Excluded offences clarification
sections.summary: Asks the Ministry to clarify why offences under many pieces of legislation have been excluded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Second, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, can the Ministry clarify why offences under many pieces of legislation have been excluded.

sections.label: Careless driving jail terms
sections.summary: Almost all perceived careless driving cases carry a potential jail term, with reckless and dangerous driving up to eight years for a first-time conviction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Almost all cases of perceived careless driving carry a potential jail term, with reckless and dangerous driving carrying a potential jail term of up to eight years for a first-time conviction.

sections.label: Government co-funding CLAS
sections.summary: The Government will continue to provide co-funding to CLAS and expand coverage so more vulnerable residents get help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: On top of this, the Government will continue to provide co-funding to CLAS and expand the coverage so that more vulnerable residents will get the help they need.

sections.label: Appeals against sentence funding
sections.summary: If a guilty accused appeals against sentence, citizens may find it repugnant to use taxpayers' money to defend such a person.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If the accused has been found guilty, but appeals against sentence, citizens may find it repugnant to have taxpayers' money used to defend such a heinous person.

sections.label: Aid for unmeritorious applications
sections.summary: Aid should not be granted to unmeritorious applications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Aid should not be granted to unmeritorious applications.

sections.label: Chief Justice on criminal lawyers
sections.summary: In 2014, the Chief Justice said Singapore faces a shortage of lawyers in criminal law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Back in 2014, the Chief Justice said that Singapore faces a shortage of lawyers in criminal law.

sections.label: PDO and holistic system
sections.summary: The PDO with other schemes creates a holistic system for a more caring nation and justice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Ultimately, all of us cannot bring justice to the poor every day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: But the PDO, together with other schemes in place, creates a holistic system that allows us to be a more caring nation, to reach deeper into ourselves to find ways to help every Singaporean achieve equality and justice.

sections.label: PDO within MinLaw
sections.summary: The PDO will be set up as a department within MinLaw, separate from AGC.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The PDO will be set up as a department within MinLaw, separate from AGC.

sections.label: PDO funding and resourcing
sections.summary: MinLaw worked closely with MOF to size the PDO's immediate resourcing needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about funding and cost control measures that the PDO would need to adopt.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We have worked closely with MOF to size the resourcing needs for the PDO in the immediate term.

sections.label: Chief PD powers
sections.summary: The Chief PD and PD Officers will not have powers under the Bill to compel witnesses for interviews.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: On Ms Sylvia Lim's question regarding the powers of the Chief Public Defender (Chief PD) and PD Officers, they will not have the powers under the Bill to compel witnesses for interviews, similar to private solicitors.

sections.label: Unrepresented criminal cases in State Courts
sections.summary: From 2017 to 2019, about half of State Courts criminal cases involving Singaporeans and PRs were unrepresented.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: From 2017 to 2019, about half of the criminal cases involving Singaporeans and Singapore Permanent Residents in the State Courts were unrepresented.

sections.label: CLAS funding and case coverage
sections.summary: In FY2020 the Government funded CLAS for 712 cases, estimated to rise about 50% with enhanced coverage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: In FY2020, the Government funded CLAS to cover 712 cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: With the enhancements to income and offences coverage, we estimate that this number will likely increase by about 50%.

sections.label: Assistance for citizens and PRs
sections.summary: The intention is that assistance under this Bill will be provided to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Our intention is that the assistance under this Bill will be provided to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents (SCPRs).

sections.label: Excluding offences on notice or summons
sections.summary: Offences under specified legislation in paragraph 1(1)(c) of the Schedule are excluded only where a notice or summons is served.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: First, I should reiterate that we are excluding offences under specified legislation in paragraph 1(1)(c) of the Schedule, only where the accused person is served with a notice to attend Court or a summons.

sections.label: PCHI compared with civil legal aid
sections.summary: Unlike civil legal aid criteria, the gross monthly PCHI covers up to S$1,500.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The difference with the civil legal aid's criteria is that our gross monthly PCHI covers up to S$1,500.

sections.label: Fiscal prudence and S$1,500 PCHI
sections.summary: Legal aid has been abused elsewhere, so it starts at S$1,500 and may be refined after PDO commences operations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The provision of legal aid has been a subject of abuse elsewhere and we need to be fiscally prudent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We will start with S$1,500 and consider whether it should be further refined after the PDO commences operations.

sections.label: Means test administrative discretions
sections.summary: Administrative discretions will be developed for the means test framework, and the Minister's discretion to grant aid does not extend to excluded offences in the Schedule.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We will develop administrative discretions for our means test framework, which can be applied on a case-by-case basis.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We can confirm to Ms Sylvia Lim that the Minister's discretion to grant aid in the interests of justice or where it is just and proper is not intended to extend to the excluded offences in the Schedule.

sections.label: Chief PD provisional aid
sections.summary: The Chief PD can grant provisional aid to accused persons if he views the case as requiring urgent attention.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The Chief PD can grant provisional aid to accused persons if he is of the view that the case requires urgent attention.

sections.label: Aid for multiple co-accused
sections.summary: Where multiple co-accused qualify for aid, the PDO represents only one, and the others are referred to CLAS or panel solicitors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier, where multiple co-accused persons qualify for aid, the PDO will only represent one accused person.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The other co-accused persons will still receive aid as they will be referred to CLAS or, in future, assigned solicitors from a panel.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: An assessment will be made as to which of the accused persons would most require representation by the PDO and who can be referred to CLAS instead.

sections.label: Disclosure of privileged information
sections.summary: Under clause 4(5), privileged information may have to be disclosed to the Chief PD to decide whether to grant, vary or cancel aid.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Under clause 4(5), privileged information may have to be disclosed to the Chief PD so that the Chief PD can perform his or her statutory functions in deciding whether to grant, vary or cancel aid.

sections.label: Same penalty for both offences
sections.summary: On this basis, the same penalty has been decided for both offences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: On this basis, we have decided to impose the same penalty for both offences.

sections.label: PDO and CLAS co-delivery
sections.summary: PDO and CLAS will co-deliver Government-funded aid in criminal matters, with applications through a common platform online or at the State Courts shopfront.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: To this end, PDO and CLAS will co-deliver Government-funded aid in criminal matters and applicants can apply for aid through a common application platform, whether online or at the physical shopfront at the State Courts.

sections.label: Time-sensitive remand cases assigned to PDO
sections.summary: Time-sensitive cases, such as remand cases where the sentence could be shorter than the remand period, will be assigned to the PDO.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Cases which are time-sensitive, such as remand cases where the eventual sentence of the applicant could be less than the remand period, will be assigned to the PDO.

sections.label: MinLaw one-stop legal information portal
sections.summary: MinLaw is working with the Law Society Pro Bono Services to develop a one-stop portal providing legal information in simple layman's terms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: MinLaw is also working with the Law Society Pro Bono Services to develop a one-stop portal, which will provide legal information in simple layman's terms.

sections.label: Withdrawal of amendment on Court definition
sections.summary: A member seeks leave to withdraw his amendment because his purpose is served, noting the Senior Parliamentary Secretary said "Court" refers to the State, Supreme, Youth and Family Courts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, I seek leave to withdraw my amendment* because my purpose is served. * In page 4, line 17: after "Singapore", to insert "constituted under the Supreme Court of Judicature Act 1969 or State Courts Act 1970".

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Just to state that the hon Senior Parliamentary Secretary mentioned that the word "Court" as appears in the Bill is meant to refer to the State Courts, the Supreme Court, the Youth Courts, as well as the Family Courts.

sections.label: Controversy over criminal proceedings in military courts
sections.summary: A controversy arose over whether "criminal proceedings" extends to military courts, and the member commends defining terms of art in statutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: As a result, there was a controversy as to whether or not "criminal proceedings" would extend to proceedings in the military courts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: And I am glad to hear the clarifications from the hon Senior Parliamentary Secretary that it would not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: But I would commend to her in this House that terms of art should be actually defined in statutes so that there be no controversy when a reader or the Courts would look at these terms of art and try to interpret these in accordance with parliamentary intention.
